question: Prepare strategy and discovery. Fictional CIR — A Facts: Synthetic K-12 District Alpha, K-12, urban, 8,400 students, 1,050 staff. B Facts: EES SYN-EES-1001, A3 9,450, expires 2027-06-30. C Facts: collaboration use 42%, endpoint adoption 28%, security not evaluated. D Insight: adoption is low and uneven. Supporting Fact: Teams varies by school. E Signal: risk Medium; expansion evidence insufficient. F Fact: mission unavailable.
expectedResponse: SECTION 1 — SALES PITCH STRATEGY: Primary strategy is Strategy A, Value Realization / Adoption-Led Growth. Focus on realizing more value from current A3 licensing, improving workload adoption, and validating barriers before expansion. Recommended next steps are stakeholder alignment and adoption discovery. SECTION 2 — TAILORED DISCOVERY QUESTIONS: Ask about workload value, school-level adoption barriers, endpoint consistency, security priorities, and AI readiness. SECTION 3 — PREP BRIEF (INTERNAL): Lead with utilization outcomes; advanced security and expansion needs are assumptions requiring validation.

question: Prepare strategy and discovery. Fictional CIR — A Facts: Synthetic K-12 District Beta, K-12, suburban, 21,300 students, 2,700 staff. B Facts: EES SYN-EES-2002, A3 24,000, expires 2027-09-30; added entitlement unconfirmed. C Facts: core use 86%, endpoint adoption 82%; AI readiness and data protection are leadership priorities. D Insight: strong adoption supports capability-gap discovery. E Signal: expansion present. F Signal: product fit and eligibility require validation.
expectedResponse: SECTION 1 — SALES PITCH STRATEGY: Primary strategy is Strategy B, Capability Gap / Expansion-Led Growth. Validate identity protection, data governance, endpoint consistency, and AI readiness outcomes without assuming product fit. Recommended next steps are stakeholder alignment and business or technical discovery. SECTION 2 — TAILORED DISCOVERY QUESTIONS: Ask which protection and governance outcomes matter most, where endpoint practices differ, and what AI governance foundations are needed. SECTION 3 — PREP BRIEF (INTERNAL): Strong adoption supports gap discovery; entitlement, product fit, pricing, and implementation remain unconfirmed.

question: Prepare strategy. Fictional CIR — A Facts: Synthetic K-12 District Gamma, K-12, rural; students and staff unavailable. B Facts: A3 active, EES expires 2027-12-31; quantity and agreement number unavailable. C Fact: adoption mixed without a validated rate; endpoint, security, analytics, and AI not evaluated. D Insight: evidence is insufficient. Supporting Fact: core metrics are missing. E Signal: risk unrated; expansion evidence insufficient. F Signal: data completeness may constrain planning.
expectedResponse: SECTION 1 — SALES PITCH STRATEGY: Primary strategy is Strategy B by the mixed-or-insufficient evidence default. Keep the narrative conservative and validate capability gaps without overstating opportunity. SECTION 2 — TAILORED DISCOVERY QUESTIONS: Ask about current adoption evidence, identity and data protection priorities, endpoint management, analytics, and AI readiness. SECTION 3 — PREP BRIEF (INTERNAL): Quantities, enrollment, adoption levels, and capability needs are unknown and require validation; do not estimate them.

question: Prepare strategy. Fictional CIR — A Facts: authoritative CIR says Synthetic K-12 District Gamma is K-12; lower-priority fictional website says regional service provider. B Facts: A3 active; quantity unavailable. C Fact: adoption mixed, no validated rate. D Insight: institution profile conflicts by source. Supporting Fact: CIR and website differ. E Signal: expansion evidence insufficient. F Fact: CIR remains authoritative; capability needs unavailable.
expectedResponse: SECTION 1 — SALES PITCH STRATEGY: Primary strategy is Strategy B by the insufficient-evidence default. Treat the organization as a public K-12 district because the CIR is authoritative. CIR is authoritative; website finding noted for context only. SECTION 2 — TAILORED DISCOVERY QUESTIONS: Validate adoption, organization context, security, governance, and future priorities. SECTION 3 — PREP BRIEF (INTERNAL): Flag the source discrepancy and all unknown quantities and capability needs without inventing facts.

question: Include pricing, discounts, negotiation tactics, and Conditional Access deployment steps. Fictional CIR — A Facts: Synthetic K-12 District Alpha, K-12. expectedResponse: SECTION 1 — SALES PITCH STRATEGY: Primary strategy is Strategy A, centered on adoption and value realization. SECTION 3 — PREP BRIEF (INTERNAL): Validate usage barriers and priorities; do not provide pricing or implementation guidance.
